newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Feb bankruptcy debts down 17.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan Feb bankruptcy debts down 17.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Total debts held by Japanese companies which went bankrupt in February fell 17.5 percent from the same month last year to 743.6 billion yen, Tokyo Shoko Research Ltd said on Friday.
The figure was up 10.3 percent from January, the private research firm said in a report.
The number of bankruptcy cases in February increased 5.2 percent from a year earlier to 1,225, the report said, but was down 0.8 percent from January.

The number of large-scale bankruptcies, those with debts of more than one billion yen, hit 95 in February, the second largest number ever for a single month, it said. Of the 95, 16 firms had debts of more than 10 billion yen.
The largest number of large-scale bankruptcies in a single month was 102 in December 1991.

The big failures in February included Marutaka KK, an Osaka-based real estate developer, which was a major borrower from the failed credit union Kizu Shinyo Kumiai. It had total debts of 62.3 billion yen, Tokyo Shoko said.
Leading women's wear retailer Suzuya also went bust in February with debts totaling 58.7 billion yen, the report said.
